summary: An elderly obese woman with HFpEF (diastolic CHF, EF>55%), paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, sick sinus syndrome s/p dual-lead pacemaker, myasthenia gravis, seizure disorder and dementia presents days after discharge with severe dyspnea, orthopnea, JVP to the earlobe, 4+ lower extremity/sacral edema, crackles, and CXR showing pulmonary edema with bilateral pleural effusions. ProBNP 4640, troponin negative, TTE with preserved EF>55%, dilated RA/RV, RAP ≥15 mmHg and mild pulmonary hypertension. She required BiPAP in the CCU, was diuresed with IV Lasix then torsemide (weight 116.4 → 108.1 kg), with rising creatinine to 1.6 (baseline 1.1) consistent with cardiorenal acute kidney injury; myasthenia and myoclonic jerks were evaluated by neurology and EEG showed no seizures.
most_likely: Acute on chronic diastolic (HFpEF) congestive heart failure exacerbation

differential.diagnosis: Acute on chronic diastolic (HFpEF) congestive heart failure exacerbation
supporting_evidence: Dyspnea, orthopnea, JVP to earlobe, 4+ pitting edema
CXR: pulmonary edema, bilateral pleural effusions, cardiomegaly
proBNP 4640; TTE EF>55%, RAP ≥15 mmHg
Diuresed IV Lasix → torsemide, weight 116.4 → 108.1 kg
opposing_evidence: ProBNP lower than prior admission value of 9682
differential.reasoning: Classic volume-overload presentation with preserved EF, imaging and biomarker support, and clear diuretic-driven hospital course; this is the principal disease treated.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury on chronic kidney disease, cardiorenal syndrome
supporting_evidence: Admission creatinine 1.4, discharge 1.6, baseline 1.1
BUN 32 at discharge; note states 'cardiorenal in setting of under-diuresis'
Apixaban renally dosed at 2.5 mg BID
opposing_evidence: No oliguria or electrolyte derangement documented
differential.reasoning: Documented rise above baseline creatinine attributed to cardiorenal physiology during aggressive diuresis; strongly codeable secondary/complication.

differential.diagnosis: Myasthenia gravis with respiratory muscle weakness contributing to dyspnea
supporting_evidence: Serial NIF measurements ~-30, lowest -22
Neurology consulted for myoclonic jerks and diaphragmatic irritation
Home pyridostigmine continued
opposing_evidence: NIF attributed mainly to poor effort; no medication change made
differential.reasoning: Active neuromuscular contributor evaluated and monitored this stay, though without documented exacerbation or treatment escalation.

differential.diagnosis: Paroxysmal atrial fibrillation with pacemaker-dependent ventricular pacing
supporting_evidence: EKG V-paced with probable underlying atrial fibrillation, 100% V-pacing
Continued apixaban 2.5 mg BID, telemetry monitoring
Prior ICD I480 and sick sinus syndrome s/p PPM
opposing_evidence: No rate-control agents required; rhythm not the driver of admission
differential.reasoning: Chronic arrhythmia actively managed and anticoagulated this stay; a contributing but not principal diagnosis.

differential.diagnosis: Acute delirium superimposed on Alzheimer's dementia
supporting_evidence: Discharge exam AAOx2, sundowning during day
Seroquel 25 mg QHS PRN started; transitional issue mentions delirium
EEG showed mildly slow background suggesting mild encephalopathy
differential.reasoning: Documented acute confusional change on a dementia background requiring pharmacologic and non-pharmacologic management.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic venous stasis with lipodermatosclerosis and MSSA-colonized leg wounds
supporting_evidence: Weeping erythematous legs, unroofed blisters healing
Wound culture: Staph aureus coag positive, sparse growth
Wound care consult, aquaphor BID PRN; prior varicose veins with inflammation
opposing_evidence: No antibiotics given; no cellulitis, fever, or leukocytosis
differential.reasoning: Real active skin problem addressed this stay but explicitly judged not a clinically significant infection.

differential.diagnosis: Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease
supporting_evidence: Lisinopril increased 2.5 → 5 mg daily this admission
LVH on TTE; SBP 120-147 on discharge
Prior ICD I129 hypertensive CKD
opposing_evidence: No hypertensive urgency or end-organ crisis this stay
differential.reasoning: Longstanding hypertension underpinning HFpEF and CKD, actively titrated during the admission.

differential.diagnosis: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure requiring noninvasive ventilation
supporting_evidence: Brought by EMS on non-rebreather for hypoxia and tachypnea
Initiated on BiPAP in the CCU; RR up to 23
differential.reasoning: BiPAP use and pre-hospital non-rebreather support a respiratory failure code, but gas exchange values were near normal after treatment.

supporting_evidence: Fleeting 'little chest pains'; new TWI V4-V6 on EKG
opposing_evidence: Prior cath with minimal non-obstructive CAD
differential.reasoning: Considered given chest discomfort and repolarization changes, but negative biomarkers and known minimal CAD make it very unlikely.

differential.diagnosis: Pulmonary embolism as cause of acute dyspnea
supporting_evidence: History of prior pulmonary embolism; dilated RV on TTE
opposing_evidence: Therapeutic on apixaban; prior CTA negative for PE
Findings fully explained by volume overload
differential.reasoning: Anticoagulated with an alternative explanation for dyspnea; listed only for completeness.

rule_outs.why: NIF around -30 attributed to effort, no bulbar weakness, no immunotherapy or intubation required.
Afebrile, WBC 3.9-6.4, CXR findings consistent with edema and effusions, no antibiotics given.
UA negative for nitrite and leukocyte esterase, urine culture no growth despite foley and bladder spasms.
EEG showed no epileptiform features or electrographic seizures despite myoclonic jerks.
TTE showed only trivial to very small circumferential effusion with no echocardiographic signs of tamponade.

uncertain_areas: Whether documentation supports coding acute hypoxemic respiratory failure given BiPAP use but normal ABG
Whether the MSSA wound growth was coded as a skin infection or as colonization only
Degree of chronic kidney disease staging versus pure acute kidney injury
Whether delirium was formally documented as a discharge diagnosis versus dementia alone
Whether myasthenia gravis was coded with or without acute exacerbation
